camera.motion: static (consecutive-frame mean abs diff of whole frame <= 0.05 grey levels; background identical every frame apart from the bird and its shadow)
camera.perspective: Background is a flat backdrop image of a building facade at night (rows of windows, neon sign BE DIFFERENT) seen frontally, with the vertical facade edges converging slightly (photo perspective, upward view). No ground plane or horizon visible. The bird flies in front of this backdrop; it casts a shadow on the backdrop at take-off, so it starts near the wall.

objects.name: bird
objects.kind: flying bird (dark, pigeon/crow-like, short beak, flapping wings)
objects.identify: the only moving object; near-black silhouette, faint red/orange highlights over dark windows
objects.reference_point: cx,cy = centroid of segmented mask (proxy for the rig root/body centre; wing flapping moves it by a few px)

objects.name: bird_shadow
objects.identify: soft dark patch on the facade left of / below the bird, frames 0-~12, merges with bird frames 0-2, drifts up-left (x~180-200, y 800->690 then fades by x~130,y~650)

objects.name: building_facade_windows
objects.identify: backdrop: grid of dark rectangular windows with orange-lit wall; left part shows a side facade lit orange

objects.name: window_ledge_takeoff
objects.identify: sloped dark window sill where the bird first appears

events.event: bird first visible (head/beak at window ledge), take-off
bird separates from its wall shadow
bird reaches top of its arc (min image y), flight turns from rising to descending
still flying at end of clip, not leaving frame
